filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
filmhouse.description: Haru, a competitive ballroom dancer in Tokyo, finds her world shattered when a sudden tragedy takes her husband-cum-dance partner from her side. Withdrawn into deep isolation and grief, she slowly allows her friends to coax her back onto the floor, where an unexpected connection with a new instructor reignites her passion. As she navigates life after loss, Haru stumbles through awkward choices, finding that healing is an exuberant, messy, and wildly colorful process. Featuring a charismatic lead performance by Rinko Kikuchi(Pacific Rim), the film presents an energetic, unabashed and fantastical way of moving on. In Japanese, Spanish and English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scene and Mature Content.

filmhouse.title: Before Sunrise
filmhouse.description: An unexpected meeting on a train leads two travelers to spend an evening wandering through Vienna. As the night unfolds, they share stories and conversations about life and love, exploring new ideas while a quiet intimacy grows between them, knowing it may be their only night together. In English. Rated NC16.

filmhouse.title: The Big Lebowski
filmhouse.description: Jeffrey 'The Dude' Lebowski, a Los Angeles slacker who only wants to bowl and drink White Russians, is mistaken for another Jeffrey Lebowski, a wheelchair-bound millionaire, and finds himself dragged into a strange series of events involving nihilists, adult film producers, ferrets, errant toes, and large sums of money. In English. Rated M18 for Coarse Language Come dressed as your favourite Lebowski character and get 10% off at the bar

filmhouse.title: Before Sunset
filmhouse.description: Nine years after their chance encounter in Vienna, American author Jesse and French environmentalist Céline cross paths once more in a Paris bookstore on the final leg of Jesse’s European book tour. With barely an hour before Jesse must catch his flight back to the United States, the pair wander through sunlit Parisian alleyways, quiet cafes, and a barge along the Seine. As their casual catch-up unfolds in near real-time, playful conversation rapidly gives way to an intimate confrontation with lost time, unfulfilled promises, and the quiet regrets of adulthood. Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, Richard Linklater’s second entry in his seminal Before trilogy is a masterpiece of naturalistic, dialogue-driven cinema. Co-written by Linklater, Ethan Hawke, and Julie Delpy, the film builds extraordinary emotional tension through razor-sharp honesty, precise pacing, and effortless chemistry between its leads. In English. Rated NC16.

filmhouse.title: The Day Iceland Stood Still
filmhouse.description: When 90% of the women of Iceland walked off the job and out of their homes one fall morning in 1975 refusing to work, cook, or take care of the children, they brought their country to a standstill and catapulted Iceland to the “best place in the world to be a woman.” Told for the first time by the women themselves, and laced with playful animation, the story is subversive and unexpectedly funny. “ We loved our male chauvinist pigs ,” recalls one of the activists, “We just wanted to change them a little!” Directed by Emmy award-winning US filmmaker Pamela Hogan in collaboration with acclaimed Icelandic producer Hrafnhildur Gunnarsdóttir, and perfectly timed for release in the lead-up to the strike’s 50th anniversary, The Day Iceland Stood Still inspires viewers to reimagine the possible In English Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language. Presented at Filmhouse as part of the Nordic Film Festival, in partnership with the Embassy of Iceland.

filmhouse.title: Perfect Days
filmhouse.description: Hirayama works as a cleaner of public toilets in Tokyo, leading a quiet, contentment-driven life structured around classic rock cassettes, secondhand books, and photographing the light filtering through urban trees. As small, unexpected encounters break his daily routine, quiet details of his past gradually come to light. Directed by Wim Wenders, this Oscar nominee for Best International Feature earned Kōji Yakusho the Best Actor prize at the Cannes Film Festival. Celebrating the dignity of labor and the art of mindfulness, the film offers a warm, contemplative, and visually striking observation of contemporary Tokyo. In Japanese with English subitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity

filmhouse.title: Fargo (30th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Jerry, a small-town Minnesota car salesman is bursting at the seams with debt... but he's got a plan. He's going to hire two thugs to kidnap his wife in a scheme to collect a hefty ransom from his wealthy father-in-law. It's going to be a snap and nobody's going to get hurt... until people start dying. Enter Police Chief Marge, a coffee-drinking, parka-wearing - and extremely pregnant - investigator who'll stop at nothing to get her man. And if you think her small-time investigative skills will give the crooks a run for their ransom... you betcha! In English Rated M18 for Violence.

filmhouse.title: Aftersun
filmhouse.description: On a quiet summer holiday at a Turkish resort in the late 1990s, 11-year-old Sophie spends precious days with her loving, idealistic father, Calum. Decades later, an adult Sophie revisits home video footage and fragmented memories from the trip, attempting to reconcile the father she remembered with the personal struggles he kept hidden from view. Charlotte Wells’ remarkable debut feature earned Paul Mescal an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor alongside the French Touch Prize at the Cannes Film Festival. A deeply felt portrait of memory, grief, and parental love, the film pairs subtle visual storytelling with remarkable central performances that linger long after the credits roll. In English. Rated M18 for Mature Content. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audiences are advised.

filmhouse.title: The Invite
filmhouse.description: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

Featuring a charismatic lead performance by Rinko Kikuchi(Pacific Rim), the film presents an energetic, unabashed and fantastical way of moving on. In Japanese, Spanish and English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scene and Mature Content.

filmhouse.title: Stalker
filmhouse.description: A faithful stalker guides a melancholic writer and a skeptical scientist into the Zone, a stretch of heavily guarded land where the ordinary laws of physics no longer apply. At its centre lies a room said to grant a person's deepest, innermost desires. Tarkovsky's most well known masterpiece, Stalker, turns the spectacle of the Zone into an introspection for the three men inside it. In this liminal nothingness, the camera lingers on moss and rust and water until stillness feels comfortable. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness ’ In Russian with English subtitles. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: Red Stars Upon the Field
filmhouse.description: When a mysterious skeleton surfaces from an East German moor, three dark chapters of German history collide: Was it a Wehrmacht deserter in 1944, a desperate farmer during GDR times or a shadowy figure of the RAF terrorism era? While hiding from her own activist past, a young woman begins to investigate, only to find herself entangled in a web of historical secrets that mirror her present struggles In German with English subtitles. Rating M18. Sexual Scene Presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore in collaboration with Filmhouse TW: Contains scenes of animal cruelty.

filmhouse.title: Digger
filmhouse.description: Digger Rockwell (Tom Cruise) is a megalomaniacal oil tycoon and one of the most powerful men on the planet. When his reckless deep-sea drilling operation in Greenland triggers a catastrophic environmental disaster, Digger refuses to back down or accept blame. Instead, he launches a frantic, delusional public relations crusade to spin the catastrophe, attempting to convince an unraveling world that he is humanity’s ultimate savior before the consequences of his hubris destroy everything. Four-time Academy Award winner Alejandro González Iñárritu ( Birdman , The Revenant ) returns to English language filmmaking with a blistering, absurdist black comedy. Anchored by Cruise’s most unhinged, transformative lead performance in decades, the film features a stellar supporting ensemble including Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons. Shot entirely on 35mm VistaVision by master cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, Digger pairs razor sharp political satire with sweeping visual scale, an audacious, large-format spectacle engineered specifically for the big screen experience. In English with English & Chinese subtitles Rated M18 for Coarse Language.

filmhouse.description: Tilda Swinton stars as Jessica, a Scottish orchid farmer in Colombia who wakes one morning to a loud, inexplicable bang that only she can hear. Her search for its origin leads her through a sound studio, a tunnel, and a stranger who seems to carry the memories of everyone before him. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness ’ In Spanish and English, with English subtitles. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: Cinema Paradiso
filmhouse.description: The ultimate love letter to moviegoing comes to Filmhouse in luminous 4K! Set in a sun-drenched Sicilian village, Giuseppe Tornatore’s timeless masterpiece follows young Salvatore as he discovers the magic of cinema inside his local picture house, guided by the wise and grumpy projectionist Alfredo (Philippe Noiret). Presented as the Oscar-winning International Theatrical Cut—gloriously restored in 4K—this quintessential ode to youth, lost love, and silver-screen magic features Ennio Morricone’s most heart-swelling, immortal score. In Italian with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual References.

filmhouse.title: No Country for Old Men
filmhouse.description: Llewelyn Moss stumbles upon dead bodies, $2 million and a hoard of heroin in a Texas desert, but methodical killer Anton Chigurh comes looking for it, with local sheriff Ed Tom Bell hot on his trail. The roles of prey and predator blur as the violent pursuit of money and justice collide. In English. Rated NC16 for Violence.

filmhouse.title: Mean Girls
filmhouse.description: Mean Girls Day Special Screening "On October 3rd, he asked me what day it was. It's October 3rd." Get in loser, we're going to the cinema. To celebrate the official holy day of the Burn Book calendar, we are bringing this modern cult classic back to the big screen! Round up your Plastics, and get a 10% discount at the bar if you dress in pink (even if it’s not a Wednesday). Grool? Grool. Raised in the African bush by her zoologist parents, home-schooled teenager Cady Heron (Lindsay Lohan) enters the ruthless social ecosystem of an American high school for the very first time. Recruited by a pair of cynical outsiders to infiltrate "The Plastics", a gilded, dictatorial clique led by the merciless Regina George (Rachel McAdams), Cady sets out to destroy their supremacy from within, only to find herself slowly seduced by the intoxicating power of popularity. Scripted with razor-sharp wit by Tina Fey, Mean Girls remains the definitive teen comedy of the 2000s, a biting, endlessly quotable satire of high-school tribalism that hasn't lost an ounce of its venom or charm. In English. Rated NC16: Some sexual references

filmhouse.title: Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust
filmhouse.description: Set in a future gothic wasteland where ancient vampires dominate a fading world, "D" a half vampire, half human bounty hunter is hired to retrieve a wealthy family's daughter abducted by a powerful vampire nobleman. Racing against the ruthless Markus Brothers, a rival band of mercenary hunters, D encounters a complex web of forbidden romance, tragic monstrousness, and dark fantasy. Widely regarded as Kawajiri’s directorial masterpiece, Bloodlust showcases the artistry of pre digital, hand drawn Japanese animation with its blend of Baroque grandeur, dark romanticism, and dazzling action choreography. The 2K restoration elevates Yoshitaka Amano's breathtaking character designs and painterly background art, restoring the film's velvet shadow tones and fine line work to pristine quality In Japanese with English subtitles. Rating TBA. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.

filmhouse.title: The Big Lebowski
filmhouse.description: Jeffrey 'The Dude' Lebowski, a Los Angeles slacker who only wants to bowl and drink White Russians, is mistaken for another Jeffrey Lebowski, a wheelchair-bound millionaire, and finds himself dragged into a strange series of events involving nihilists, adult film producers, ferrets, errant toes, and large sums of money. In English. Rated M18 for Coarse Language Come dressed as your favourite Lebowski character and get 10% off at the bar

filmhouse.title: Yellow Letters
filmhouse.description: Life is good for Derya and Aziz, a celebrated artist couple from Turkey, until an incident at their play’s premiere. Suddenly targeted by the state and struggling to balance their ideals with life’s necessities, their marriage is pushed to a breaking point. In Turkish with English subtitles. Rating PG. Some Coarse Language Presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore in collaboration with Filmhouse

filmhouse.title: Cyber City Oedo 808
filmhouse.description: In a dystopian 29th-century Tokyo, three hardened criminals, Sengoku, Gogul, and Benten are released from an orbital prison to serve as a high tech penal police force. Outfitted with explosive collars that detonate if they disobey, the trio is dispatched to hunt down lethal cyber terrorists, rogue Androids, and mutated corporate experiments in exchange for reductions in their century long sentences. A foundational pillar of 1990s anime cyberpunk, Kawajiri’s signature neon noir aesthetic, fluid kinetic violence, and intricate mechanical designs by Takashi Watabe (Akira) directly influenced Western sci-fi landmarks like The Matrix. In its 2K restoration, the film’s striking hand drawn cel animation, rich shadow work, and vivid cyberpunk palette pop with high definition clarity *The original 3-Part OVA will be shown in one continuous sitting. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rating TBA. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audience are advised.

filmhouse.title: Ratatouille
filmhouse.description: In the high-stakes culinary capital of Paris, Remy, a gifted rat with an extraordinarily refined palate, dreams of becoming a master chef despite the obvious hazards of his species. After accidentally arriving at the legendary Gusteau’s restaurant, he forms an unlikely partnership with Linguini, a clumsy kitchen garbage boy with zero culinary skills. Hiding beneath Linguini’s chef hat and pulling his hair like a puppeteer, Remy crafts exquisite dishes that captivate the city, all while dodging an scheming head chef and Paris’s most dreaded food critic, Anton Ego. Winner of the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, Brad Bird’s Pixar masterpiece is a brilliant, kinetic tribute to French gastronomy and the transformative power of art. Elevated by Michael Giacchino’s iconic, jazz-infused score and breathtaking visual detail, the film balances slapstick physical comedy with a deeply resonant message on talent, passion, and perseverance. A perennial audience favorite that appeals equally to families, cinephiles, and food lovers! In English. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: Before Sunset
filmhouse.description: Nine years after their chance encounter in Vienna, American author Jesse and French environmentalist Céline cross paths once more in a Paris bookstore on the final leg of Jesse’s European book tour. With barely an hour before Jesse must catch his flight back to the United States, the pair wander through sunlit Parisian alleyways, quiet cafes, and a barge along the Seine. As their casual catch-up unfolds in near real-time, playful conversation rapidly gives way to an intimate confrontation with lost time, unfulfilled promises, and the quiet regrets of adulthood. Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, Richard Linklater’s second entry in his seminal Before trilogy is a masterpiece of naturalistic, dialogue-driven cinema. Co-written by Linklater, Ethan Hawke, and Julie Delpy, the film builds extraordinary emotional tension through razor-sharp honesty, precise pacing, and effortless chemistry between its leads. In English. Rated NC16.

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Aftersun
filmhouse.description: On a quiet summer holiday at a Turkish resort in the late 1990s, 11-year-old Sophie spends precious days with her loving, idealistic father, Calum. Decades later, an adult Sophie revisits home video footage and fragmented memories from the trip, attempting to reconcile the father she remembered with the personal struggles he kept hidden from view. Charlotte Wells’ remarkable debut feature earned Paul Mescal an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor alongside the French Touch Prize at the Cannes Film Festival. A deeply felt portrait of memory, grief, and parental love, the film pairs subtle visual storytelling with remarkable central performances that linger long after the credits roll. In English. Rated M18 for Mature Content. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audiences are advised.

filmhouse.title: A Poet
filmhouse.description: Oscar is an aging, rueful poet whose artistic ambitions have long faded into obscurity and heavy drinking. When Oscar takes up teaching to meet ends meet, he encounters Yurlady, a working-class girl with an extraordinary gift for poetry, he becomes consumed with launching her talent into the local literary scene. Driven by a desperate longing for career redemption and a second chance at fatherhood, Oscar inadvertently pushes her into an ambitious world she never asked to join. Directed by Simón Mesa Soto, this tragicomedy earned the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and represented Colombia as its official submission for Best International Feature Film. Anchored by a brilliant, cringe-inducing performance from Ubeimar Rios, the film offers a darkly funny and deeply humane satire on artist egos and the messy search for purpose. A Poet, A Creative, A Panel Join us for a post-show fireside chat on Tue 6 Oct, 7.30pm ! Do you dream of writing your story one day? Of writing novels, poetry, or making films? Do you want to support those dreamers around us to do so? It isn’t easy being an artist anywhere, especially not outside major commercial systems like America, the UK, and Hollywood. And though A POET comes from halfway across the world, our creative industries are really not so different. So why make the admirably Herculean task of creating any harder by keeping career wisdom behind closed doors (or gates), or by having to struggle alone? And if you care about local voices, then how can we best support our artists? Join us for a fireside chat with a local poet, Theophilus Kwek , and filmmaker, Pek Jia Hao , as they share with us their uncensored stories, tips and tricks, and dreams for the creative life in Singapore. In Spanish with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Nudity.

With the true mastermind lurking in the shadows, Lan Pui-ching must overcome the inner demons that have haunted her for 13 years and stop the next murder in a world where science and supernatural collide.

living her first date on repeat with ‘Henry’ (Nadech Kugimiya), a good-natured,

remember anything from the day before. So, Lucy has to find a way to keep
